Rohod Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Rohod, Hungary

Not demolished. Historically two separate Jewish cemeteries in Rohod, both enclosed within a single fence and marked on the 1870 cadastral map, have since effectively merged into one visible site. Population grew from 28 in 1826 to a peak of 150 by 1910, declining to 104 by 1941; the community joined the Orthodox stream in 1867 under Rabbi Jungreisz Jakab of Nyírmada. In May 1944, residents were confined to the Kisvárda Ghetto and deported to Auschwitz that same month. Descendants of former Rohod Jews continue to visit the graves regularly today.
